2026-10-20 - Uncovering the AI-Driven Offensive Infrastructure of INC and The Gentlemen Ransomware Affiliates

Research URL: https://socradar.io/blog/inc-gentlemen-ransomware-ai-infrastructure/

Key Points
- AI serves as the operational core and primary evidence corpus of the ecosystem. Operators run workflows via OpenCode and OpenRouter-hosted models, logging activity across multiple databases, 92 session files, and a knowledge base. Total AI API expenditure exceeds $23,920.
- Analysis links the infrastructure to INC and The Gentlemen Ransomware groups’ operators, and reveals that a deployment wave was staged. Operators prepared 46 INC encryptor binaries built for 6 victims - three victims hold a single standalone Windows build each, and three hold a complete 14-platform package each (one distinct X25519 keypair per victim) plus one non-personalized attacker-side cross-compile. A SimpleHelp session from 30 September confirmed active encryption. Concurrently, The Gentlemen side is a branded extortion package (four-message escalation, vishing plan) for one publicly listed victim case.
- Evidence from log files confirms widespread automated attacks focusing on public-facing devices. Documented instances include widespread compromises of FortiClient EMS deployments (CVE-2026-35616 - 2,236 discovered targets, 227 VPN profiles on 96 servers, 108 created admins, 4,140 managed endpoints), SimpleHelp infrastructure (CVE-2024-57727, impacting 242 unique IP addresses), cPanel environments (CVE-2026-41940, with 49 or more verified breaches), and per operator claims.
- Exposed servers contain the operational architecture, encompassing AI/knowledge databases, Phantom Framework, target intelligence, RevSocks, Ghost C2 delivery mechanisms, and an administrative control panel. While the exposed files provide robust evidentiary value, they do not constitute exhaustive live-service telemetry. Furthermore, the architecture utilizes distinct codebases across multiple C2 variants rather than relying on a unified backend.
- Targeting spans 62 named organizations, primarily concentrated in the United States (36 entities) and sectorally led by industrial/manufacturing (16.1%) and healthcare (14.5%).
